case: Barclays / Lehman Brothers North American operations (2008)

claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; businesses retained and integrated into Barclays Capital
claude.rationale: Section 2 documents that the customer-facing franchises (T4: FI/equities sales, trading, research, IB) transferred together with their supporting operating infrastructure — the 745 Seventh Avenue HQ and two NJ data centres (T5) — and ~10,000 employees (T6) moved into Barclays Capital as a going concern, so no product-vs-process (gap_45=0) or process-vs-organization (gap_56=0) mismatch is documented at closing. Section 4 explicitly records "None documented" for P4 (product-process) and P5 (process-organization), with product franchises, infrastructure and staff transferring together and Barclays intending rapid integration, driving p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0. The principal post-deal controversy (Section 3-4) was legal/valuation ("$11bn windfall" litigation), not an operational integration failure.

gemini.performance_metric: No divestiture — the acquired businesses were retained and integrated into Barclays Capital.
gemini.rationale: The dossier documents that the North American product franchises (T4), supporting operating infrastructure including HQ and data centres (T5), and approximately 10,000 employees (T6) transferred together as a going concern. No structural gaps between product, process, and organization were documented at closing (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). Post-deal, there is no documented disruption at the product-process interface (p4_pathway=0) or the process-organization interface (p5_pathway=0), with the businesses successfully integrated into Barclays Capital.
